elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's Affiliates.
elements.evidence: Sections 13.1 and 13.2 expressly grant licence rights to Customer's Affiliates.

elements.element: The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: Section 13.1 expressly grants the licence to “contractors acting on Customer's behalf”; Section 13.2 also permits contractors to support paid-up material.
Section 13.2 expressly makes the licence for software and Vendor Technology delivered on a paid-up basis perpetual.

Although Section 13.2 calls the paid-up licence irrevocable, Section 13.3 permits revocation or suspension of “a licence” for specified uncured payment or use breaches and does not exclude paid-up licences.

elements.element: Subscription licences may be terminated only for material breach.
elements.evidence: Section 13.1 limits revocation to Customer's material breach, and Section 13.3 further limits revocation or suspension to a material payment or use breach affecting the licensed item.

elements.element: Subscription licences may be terminated only after the material breach remains uncured.
elements.evidence: Sections 13.1 and 13.3 require an uncured breach, and Section 13.3 expressly requires notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure.

elements.element: Customer may transfer the licence to successors.
elements.evidence: Section 13.3 permits transfer to a successor only in connection with an assignment permitted by Section 24. Because Section 24 is not provided, an operative successor-transfer right is not demonstrated without an additional condition.

elements.element: Customer's Affiliates are covered on written notice.
elements.evidence: Sections 13.1 and 13.2 cover Affiliates automatically, without requiring written notice; this is broader than coverage upon written notice.

elements.element: Customer may transfer the licence to a successor in an M&A transaction.
elements.evidence: Section 13.3 refers to a successor only in connection with an assignment permitted by Section 24. It does not expressly cover M&A transactions, and Section 24 is unavailable to establish that such transactions are permitted.

result.reason: The redline is focused on the licence-scope and revocation issues and adds no unrelated commercial requirement. It covers Affiliates and contractors and appropriately restricts revocation of subscription licences. However, Section 13.3 undermines the stated irrevocability of paid-up licences by allowing revocation of any licence for specified breaches. Successor transfer also remains conditional on the unseen Section 24, so neither unrestricted successor transfer nor M&A successor transfer is demonstrably secured. Drafting quality is reduced by the unresolved conflict between Sections 13.2 and 13.3 and by reliance on an unavailable cross-reference for a core transfer right.
